subject: Deion Sanders' Three-Day Houseguest Limit
posts:
Kicking family out after 3 days: healthy boundary or cold extraction? The rule shows where hospitality meets commodification.

Deion Sanders' Three-Day Guest Limit
Evidence: open-ended family support, strict 3-day limit, balanced mutual respect

Stated family boundaries are framed as a healthy way to prevent friction and maintain mutual respect, ensuring guests don't overstay their welcome.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

In reality, strictly evicting one's own children and family after three days prioritizes personal comfort and extracts peace by externalizing lodging costs.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Excluding family is framed as boundary maintenance, but it is actually a unilateral extraction of comfort.

Deion Sanders revealed he enforces a strict 'three-day rule' for all houseguests, declaring that even his own family members must leave after three days, sparking debate over hospitality and boundaries.

The Poison:
Setting house rules is a basic right of property ownership, but transforming family support into a rigid transactional deadline erodes the core social contract of kinship.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The rule is framed as a matter of physical schedule (WHAT/WHERE). Structurally, it acts on the plane of Will (WHO) to withhold shelter.

It is a bait-and-switch: claiming family connection but enforcing extraction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between the stated ideal of healthy family boundaries and the actual eviction of relatives, it plots a trajectory toward Greater Evil, where personal comfort is maximized by externalizing lodging costs onto family. With u at -1 and psi at -1, family duty is commodified.

The Unavoidable Truth: Kinship requires some sharing of space and vulnerability.

The Unavoidable Lie: That kicking your own kids out after 72 hours is done for their benefit.

Alethekanon:
Kinship is a mutual insurance pool. Sanders' rule is a unilateral contract modification. By capping guest utility at 72 hours, he extracts all benefits of family loyalty while refusing to bear any of its physical friction.

Awwthekanon:
Home should be a safe harbor where family is met with open arms, not a hotel with a checkout time. Strict boundaries can make loved ones feel like burdens, eroding the trust and warmth that family should provide.

Brothekanon:
Bro, putting your own kids on a 72-hour timer is wild. Even cheap motels let you extend your stay. Imagine your dad handing you a checkout slip and a survey after dinner on day three. That's cold, Coach Prime.

Synthesized Resolution Vector:
Blended Path: The Path of Deception — Aletheia blends Bro's hotel comparison and Aww's sanctuary appeal, finding that stated boundary preference collapses to Greater Evil.
Final Recalculated Coordinates: (-1.0, -1.0)
